text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx (502/504) and upstream timeouts on /v1/generate in us-west1. Alert threshold exceeded (20m). Affected tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma, tenant-zeta. Estimated error rate: 18%.
oncall-maya: taking pager — onboarding. Starting with kb and recent deploys.
liam-eng: noticed spike at ~14:02 UTC. Gateway logs show rapid 502s with upstream error 'unexpected EOF' and several model-runner crashes (SIGSEGV).
ops-sre: confirming — mutli-AZ but concentrated on inference-pool-12 in us-west1-a. CPU on nodes ok, but GPU memory pressure high on a subset.
runtime-bot: autocollect: last 15m kernel logs attached: 
```
# kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 3241 (model-runner) total-vm: ...
[14:03:12] model-runner[3241]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f4a1abcde sp 0x7ff... error 4 in libattention.so
```
liam-eng: stack suggests attention kernel crash during KV-cache write. We also have long context requests from tenant-alpha (seq_len up to ~120k tokens). That would blow kv cache.
oncall-maya: load on that pool matches their traffic pattern — tenant-alpha batch windows just hit a spike.
jordan-ps: can we hot-route their requests to a fallback model (quantized smaller) while we stabilize?
ops-sre: I can add a temporary routing rule to send tenant-alpha -> model-variant:xsmall in us-west1-b. Applying now.
(ops-sre applied routing): routing-rule applied -> tenant-alpha -> xsmall (us-west1-b) : should start draining in 30s.
liam-eng: good. Next: mitigate memory pressure on inference-pool-12 — reduce batch size, disable dynamic KV growth, and restart affected runners gracefully. Suggest setting ENV MAX_KV_BYTES=2Gi and BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512.
oncall-maya: agree. ops-sre, can you push those env changes as a rolling restart?
ops-sre: rolling restart started with graceful drain. Command used: `kubectl -n inference deploy model-runner --env="MAX_KV_BYTES=2147483648" --env="BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512"` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-runner -n inference --field-selector=spec.nodeName=pool-12-node-?`
runtime-bot: noticed several runner instances still crashing during restart (exit code 139). Collecting core dumps to GCS: gs://redwood-incident-dumps/1748009123/*.core.gz
liam-eng: pulling a core — crash consistent in fused attention kernel when kv-index append hits end-of-buffer. Looks like we don't guard against extreme seq lengths in the native code path.
ops-sre: while we patch, we should enable fallback kernel that avoids the fused path (less perf but safer). There's a runtime flag `FORCE_SAFE_KERNEL=1`. Toggling on cluster.
(ops-sre): `kubectl set env deploy/model-runner FORCE_SAFE_KERNEL=1 -n inference` -> applied.
liam-eng: good. This should stop new segfaults. Queued requests may still hit timeouts while runners drain.
oncall-maya: customer-impact note: tenant-alpha saw ~27% of requests fail during spike window; tenant-gamma ~5%; tenant-zeta ~3%. CS @cs-rep please prepare communication.
cs-rep: drafting message — will send status update to tenant alpha + gamma within 30 minutes. ETA: short mitigation performed (routing to xsmall) and cluster env toggled. Asking for any data retention concerns.
jordan-ps: temporary workaround for customers: set max_input_tokens in client or enable server-side prefix truncation (we can gate with tenant flag). Ops, can we enable server-side request truncation at the gateway for very long inputs?
ops-sre: yes, adding policy `max_client_tokens=50k` for tenants without explicit opt-in. Pushing now.
(ops-sre): gateway rule pushed -> rejects >50k tokens with 413 and suggestion header `X-RW-TRUNCATE-SUGGEST: true`.
liam-eng: code patch landed to add guard in attention kernel and a unit test for extreme seq lengths. Creating hotfix build `runner:2025.11.12-hotfix-1`.
ops-sre: hotfix image built and canary deployed to 2 pods in pool-12. Monitoring.
runtime-bot: canary metrics: no crashes for 10m on canary pods, memory stable.
oncall-maya: rolling canary -> rest of pool pending cursory check.
ops-sre: full rollout started for model-runner:2025.11.12-hotfix-1. Expected complete in 6m.
liam-eng: post-rollout we should leave FORCE_SAFE_KERNEL=0 to regain perf once hotfix validated. For now keep it on.
ops-sre: rollout complete. Crash count fell to zero, gateway 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.5%.
oncall-maya: excellent. Customer impact summary for postmortem: root cause = unbounded KV-cache growth + fused attention kernel not guarding extreme seq lengths -> segfault/OOM during inference -> cascade 5xx at gateway. Contributing factors: lack of tenant-level token caps, no server-side truncation, and an unsafe kernel path for rare extreme contexts.
jordan-ps: mitigation performed: (1) emergency routing for tenant-alpha to xsmall variant, (2) gateway token cap 50k, (3) FORCE_SAFE_KERNEL enabled cluster-wide, (4) rolling restart with MAX_KV_BYTES and BATCH_MAX_TOKENS limits, (5) hotfix release with kernel guard.
oncall-maya: action items and owners:
- liam-eng: merge kernel guard to main and add stress test harness for long contexts (due EOD).
- runtime-team (liam + ops): add telemetry for per-request kv-allocation and per-tenant long-context alerts (due 2025-11-19).
- ops-sre: document rollout playbook and default gateway max_client_tokens policy (due 2025-11-14).
- cs-rep: send customer notifications & post-incident customer follow-up (due 2025-11-13).
- product: evaluate tenant opt-in model for >50k tokens and safety review.
cs-rep: sent initial status to tenant-alpha and tenant-gamma, included mitigation steps and timeline.
liam-eng: recording incident for postmortem: will attach core dumps, metrics (gateway errors, runner crashes), and the hotfix diff.
oncall-maya: closing pager — system stabilized, no regressions observed for 45m. If anything flips, re-open.
incident-bot: Pager closed by oncall-maya at 2025-11-12T15:20:30Z.
ops-sre: leaving logs and playbook links: https://confluence.redwood/internal/incidents/1748009123 and gs://redwood-incident-dumps/1748009123/
